_meta.indication: Treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) antibody positive.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, multinational study; 1:1 randomization; loading dose 30 mg/kg IV followed by 15 mg/kg Q2W or placebo over a 24-week double-blind phase, followed by an open-label extension; conducted at 82 sites in 17 countries.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult subjects with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) and MGFA Clinical Classification Class II to IV, with MG-ADL total score of at least 6, on stable standard of care MG therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: average change from baseline in MG-ADL total score over Weeks 22, 23, and 24. Key secondary: average change from baseline in QMG total score over Weeks 22 and 24.
pivotal_trials.n: 196 randomized 1:1 (IMAAVY n=98, placebo n=98); primary efficacy analysis population n=153 (IMAAVY N=77, placebo N=76).
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint met: MG-ADL LS mean change -4.7 (IMAAVY) vs -3.3 (placebo); LS mean difference -1.5 (95% CI -2.4, -0.5); p=0.002. Secondary QMG LS mean difference -2.8 (95% CI -4.2, -1.4); p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) were respiratory tract infection (18% vs 13% placebo), peripheral edema (12% vs 2%), and muscle spasm (12% vs 3%). Warnings include infections (43% of IMAAVY patients in Study 1), hypersensitivity reactions (16%), and infusion-related reactions (11%).
target_moa: Nipocalimab binds to the IgG binding site on the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) at both neutral and acidic pH to inhibit IgG recycling, reducing circulating IgG levels including pathogenic IgG (anti-AChR and anti-MuSK autoantibodies).
modality: mAb (human aglycosylated IgG1 lambda monoclonal antibody / FcRn blocker)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held because this biologic is not the first in its class.

summary.text: Nipocalimab received orphan drug designation (February 11, 2021) and fast track designation (December 21, 2021), and the BLA was granted priority review. Approval was based on a single adequate and well-controlled study (Study 011) with confirmatory pharmacodynamic/mechanistic evidence; this was a traditional (non-accelerated) approval and no advisory committee was convened.

requirement.text: 4833-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to lmaavy (nipocalimab) during pregnancy and lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol. The protocol must be agreed upon with the Agency.
